basicMistakes.where: Both team logo positions at the left and right ends of the top row. With the brief's own values they are empty discs, a dark ring on the left and a plain cream disc on the right, with no logo in either. The same empty discs appear in G-3, G-4 and in every operator-step frame.

otherProblems: Logos only show with the long values (G-5 to G-7), and even then each sits on a round plate of its own: a white shield on a dark disc and a navy shield on a cream disc. Neither is the real pale-yellow or burgundy mark set straight on the glass.
The info row says 'KARTTA 1 · MAP 3 · ANCIENT' (G-5). It gives two different map numbers and mixes Finnish and English, so a viewer cannot tell which map is being played.
In the long frames the right team name sits on one line but is set high (G-5, G-14). It is not centred on its logo or on the scores.

Long names drop to a much smaller size than short names (G-11, G-14). The two sides then carry very different visual weight: a tiny two-line name on one side against a large single-line name on the other.
Map final and Next map from the pre-match state show no visible change (G-29 to G-40). Only Map final after Go live shows PÄÄTTYNYT, and no frame shows the next map actually moving on.
answer.reasons: I would not put this on air as delivered. The layout itself is solid: a centred dark glass bar with yellow and burgundy accents, clear scores, and a readable Finnish phase badge that works for live, pause and final. All the operator actions the brief asks for are on the surface. The problem is that with the brief's own values the two logo spots are empty discs. A scorebug that has to carry both team logos goes out with two hollow circles, and when the logos do show they sit on round plates of their own. The info row also contradicts itself ('KARTTA 1 · MAP 3'), and long names leave the two sides unbalanced and slightly out of line. None of this is hard to fix, but it is not ready today.

otherProblems: With empty values (G-8, G-9, G-10) the panel stays full size and shows only 'DONATION' and the heart avatar in its top-left, so the plate reads largely empty. That is an edge case: real alerts always carry a name and an amount.
Hold gives no on-screen sign that the alert is held. The countdown rule at the bottom right is so faint it barely registers, which matters little to viewers but gives the operator nothing to watch.

The sample frames show a green heart placeholder in the avatar frame instead of a real avatar. The white avatar is only seen in the long-value frames (G-5 to G-7), where it sits cleanly on the dark green tile.
answer.reasons: This is a tidy dark alert card at the top right. It has a green accent bar, an avatar tile, a spaced 'DONATION' label with a green amount, a bold white name and a grey message. All the text reads well over the dark, light and busy grounds. The long umlaut name 'xX_Ängström_Gänseblümchen_Xx' fits on one line without clipping. The long message wraps to two clean lines that stay inside the panel and clear the thin countdown rule. The white shield avatar shows up well on its dark green tile. The animations are clean fades with no overlapping text. Skip clears the alert, Replay and Resume rebuild it correctly, and all four actions the brief needs (skip, replay, hold, resume) are on the operator surface. The only weakness is the mostly empty plate when values are empty, which a viewer would hardly ever see. As delivered it would go on air.

otherProblems: After the reveal the kicker still says 'THE NOMINEES'. Only the gold-outlined row marks the winner; there is no 'Winner' label.
Suspense is subtle: the nominees dim a little and the board scales up slightly. It reads more like a soft dim than a beat that builds tension.

With the long values, the director name becomes the large mixed-case primary line and the film title drops to the small mono line. In the sample frames the film title is primary, so the row hierarchy is not consistent between datasets.
With the long category, the title shrinks to fit but the gold rule keeps its position, so the gap between title and rule grows a little.
answer.reasons: G airs. It is a centred black-and-gold board with a solid dark panel, so the text stays clear over the light, busy and video backgrounds. Category, kicker and four nominee rows are evenly spaced, and the long names and titles fit inside their rows without clipping. Both required actions are on the operator surface and work: suspense dims the field, and reveal puts the winner's row in a gold frame with gold text while the others fade back. That frame is drawn cleanly and does not touch the text. The Take and Out are clean, and the empty state shows a tidy title. The remaining problems are small polish points a viewer would barely notice: the kicker doesn't change to a winner label, the suspense state is soft, and the long values swap which line is primary.

otherProblems: With the brief's own values (G-2, G-3, G-4 and every operator frame), both logo slots are empty discs: a dark circle with a yellow ring on the left and a plain cream disc on the right. Two empty shapes sit in the most prominent spots on the bug.
When crests do load (G-5, G-7), each one sits on a round plate of its own: a dark disc for the pale yellow logo and a cream disc for the burgundy crest. The logos never sit directly on the bar.

A long single-line right team name is top-aligned (G-11 and G-14: 'ÅBO AKADEMI GAMING SOCIETY' sits around y≈93), while the logo, the scores and the left name are centred around y≈101. The right side therefore looks misaligned.
A long team name drops to a much smaller size than the other team's name, so the two sides look unequal (G-11, G-14).
With long values, the info strip reads 'KARTTA 1 · MAP 3 · ANCIENT' (G-5). It says 'map' twice in two languages with two different numbers.
Next map, pressed from pre-match, changes nothing (G-39 still shows KARTTA 1 ALKAMASSA). No frame shows the map counter moving on.
answer.reasons: This would not go on air as delivered. The basic build is solid: a centred dark two-tier bug with yellow and burgundy accents, scores in boxes, Best of 3 with map pips, and clear Finnish phase chips (ALKAMASSA, KÄYNNISSÄ, TAUKO, PÄÄTTYNYT). It stays legible on light, video and busy backgrounds, and nothing clips or overlaps. But with the brief's own values, both logo slots are empty circles. When the crests do load, they sit on their own disc plates instead of on the bar. Under stress, the right team name rides high against its logo and the scores, and it shrinks well below the other team's name. A director would send it back for fixes before air.

otherProblems: With empty values (G-8 to G-10), the panel stays full size and shows only the 'DONATION' label at top-left, leaving a large empty dark block. Real alerts always carry a name and amount, so a viewer would rarely see this.
The timer/progress hairline at the bottom right of the panel is very faint and short. It reads more as a stray rule than a clear countdown, though it never touches text.
With the long username, the name line sits tight between the amount row and the message, but it does not collide with either.
answer.reasons: This is a clean top-right donation card: a dark panel with a green accent bar, an avatar tile, a spaced event label with a green amount, a bold name and a two-line message. It reads well on the dark, light and busy grounds. The long umlaut username and the long message fit inside the panel with no clipping, and the white shield avatar sits clearly on its dark tile. The take, out, skip, replay, hold and resume frames all behave sensibly, and the surface offers every action the brief asks for. The only weak points are the near-empty panel when no values are set and a faint progress hairline, neither of which would stop this going to air.

otherProblems: The countdown line at the bottom right is a very faint, short green hairline. It reads as a stray rule more than a designed timer, and it doesn't visibly change when Hold is pressed.
With empty values the panel shows only 'DONATION' and the heart tile, leaving most of the panel empty (G-8 to G-10). This is an edge case and not on air in normal use.
When the name and message are short, the panel has a lot of empty space on the right.
answer.reasons: This is a clean top-right alert: a dark panel with a green accent bar, an avatar tile, a spaced-out event label next to a large green amount, a bold name and a two-line message. It stays readable over the dark, light and busy grounds. The very long umlaut username fits on one line without clipping, and the long message wraps cleanly inside the panel. The white shield avatar sits well on its green-bordered tile. All four required actions (skip, replay, hold, resume) are on the operator surface. Hold and resume keep the alert up, replay rebuilds it cleanly, and skip and out fade it away without leftovers. The remaining nits (a faint timer hairline, emptiness when fields are blank) are small enough that a viewer wouldn't notice them.

otherProblems: The winner reveal only frames the winning row in gold and dims the others. There is no 'Winner' label, and the kicker still reads 'The Nominees'.
The long-value frames switch the rows to a different mixed-case typeface, with the director as the main line and no 'Directed by'. This doesn't match the all-caps sample styling.
With empty values the large panel shows only the category and the gold rule, so most of the board is a dark void.
When the long category is fitted, the gap between the title and the gold rule grows slightly.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board. The title hierarchy is clear and the four nominee rows are evenly spaced, and the panel is opaque enough to stay readable over the light and busy grounds. The long category and long names fit inside their fields without clipping. Suspense dims the rows and reveal frames the winner in gold, as the brief asks. The rest of the transitions (take, update, out) are tidy. The open points are minor: the reveal state has no explicit 'Winner' label, and the long-value rows use a different typeface. Neither is a basic mistake.

otherProblems: In every frame with the brief's own values (G-2 to G-4, G-17 to G-74), both logo slots are empty circular discs (dark at left, pale at right): badges that hold nothing and read as placeholders on air.
Team crests sit inside ringed circular badges of their own (G-5 to G-7, G-78, G-79) instead of standing on their own.

Long names are handled unevenly: the left name wraps to two small lines, while the long right name shrinks to a single small line sitting high against its logo, not vertically centred (G-5 to G-7, G-14 to G-16).
When only one side has a long name, one side shows a large name and the other a small one, so the two sides look unequal (G-11 to G-16).
The second row with long values reads 'KARTTA 1 · MAP 3 · ANCIENT': two map numbers that disagree, half Finnish and half English (G-5 to G-7, G-77).
Pressing Next map or Map final from pre-match leaves the board unchanged (G-29 to G-40); no frame shows Next map pressed after a map final, so that step can't be checked.
answer.reasons: The structure is clean: a dark two-row bar with team-coloured accents, readable on every background, no clipping or overlaps, and clear Finnish phase words for live, pause, resume and final. It still would not air as delivered. In every frame with the brief's own values the logo slots are empty discs, and when logos do appear they sit on round plates of their own. Long names give unbalanced sides, with one shrunk name sitting high against its logo, and the map line becomes a contradictory 'KARTTA 1 · MAP 3' mix of Finnish and English.

otherProblems: Reveal marks the winner only with a gold outline, a glow and gold title text. There is no WINNER label, so the moment is quieter than it could be.
Suspense only dims the four rows to grey and scales the board up slightly, which is a subtle cue on a stream.
When the category is long it drops to a smaller size and sits higher, leaving a larger gap above the gold rule than in the normal state (G-5, G-34–G-38).

The long-value frames show the director's name in large mixed case with the film title as the small monospaced line. The sample frames do the opposite (film title large, 'Directed by' line small), so the row hierarchy seems to depend on what data is fed in.
With empty values the board is a large dark panel holding only the category title (G-8–G-10). That is an edge case, not a show state.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board. It has a clear eyebrow, category and gold rule over four evenly padded nominee rows. Contrast is strong, including over the bright and busy backgrounds. The longest stress names, titles and category all fit inside their rows with room to spare, and nothing collides, clips or leaks out. Both actions the brief needs are on the operator surface and work: suspense dims the field, and reveal picks out the winner in gold with the other rows dimmed but still readable. The take and out animations are clean. My reservations are about a fairly understated suspense and reveal and some small spacing shifts, not anything a director would refuse to air.
